scope: All 35 records in the current tribunal/office inventory, using the current statutory appointment observations and a bounded review of ambiguous classes.

schedule_2a.textual_rule: A person, corporation, commission, board, bureau or authority qualifies where the person, a majority of its members, or a majority of its management/director board is appointed by an Act, a minister or the Lieutenant Governor in Council.

schedule_2b.textual_rule: The same person/majority formulation applies where those persons, in discharging their duties, are public officers or servants of the government.

schedule_2c.textual_rule: The same person/majority formulation applies where those persons are responsible to the government.

authority_includes_members_employees.textual_rule: The statutory definition of authority includes members and employees of a scheduled authority.

administrative_scope.textual_rule: The investigation power concerns administrative decisions, acts, omissions and procedures. Section 11 limits investigations while a statutory appeal, objection or merits review remains unexercised and unexpired, and excludes counsel conduct in the specified circumstances. Section 13 provides grounds to refuse or end an investigation.

methodology: Current appointment composition is the primary factual premise. A statutory majority appointed by the listed government appointors supports an explicitly labeled application of Schedule 2(a).
The legal text and the factual appointment provisions are direct evidence; matching a named body to a generic Schedule class is the researcher’s inference, not a named entry in the Act.
An elected or nominating body is not treated as the appointor when the statute gives the final appointment to a minister or Cabinet.
Chair-appointed temporary or ordinary tribunal members are not automatically treated as Cabinet-appointed members, or as appointed by an Act merely because the power appears in an Act.
A statutory person can satisfy item 2 without a board; officeholder-scoped conclusions are labeled and do not manufacture a corporate board or establish all branch functions.

The two specified express exclusions were checked before assigning any class. No one in this 35-record set is one of the excluded ferry corporations or a Police Act body under its identified enabling provisions.
The Managed Forest Council’s normal 2-of-5 ministerial appointments are not a majority, nor is statutory incorporation itself proof of government ownership.

Named Ombudsperson authority statistics and official complaint procedures are recorded independently. They can provide positive jurisdiction/route evidence even where the exact Schedule limb is unresolved.
No class is backdated to establishment, incorporation or a predecessor. All first-coverage dates remain null.
A scrutiny relationship is not a managerial accountability path and does not promise reversal of a tribunal’s decision.
